samples.summary: New image-fetch guard aborts the whole docs PDF/DOCX export when one image is refused — the exporters have no per-image catch
samples.evidence: `collectAndEmbedImages` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:57) does `const blob = await fetcher(src);` inside the loop with no try/catch, and `DocxExporter.export` does the same at packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:76. `createImageFetcher` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261) now *throws* for any image whose host is non-public or whose scheme is not http/https/data, where previously it only threw on a non-OK HTTP status. So a self-hosted install serving blobs from an internal host (MinIO, a second port on the API box), or a doc carrying an intranet/`file:`-style `src` from an import, turns `wafflebase docs export` from "PDF with a missing/failed image" into "whole export fails" — and the CLI has no `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS` set by default. Note the inconsistency: the slides PDF path *does* swallow per-image failures (packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:282-284), so the same guarded refusal degrades gracefully there and is fatal in docs. Fix belongs either in the new fetcher (skip vs. throw policy) or in the docs exporters.

samples.summary: `seg()` makes `fileUrl` throw synchronously inside a React render path, turning a bad route id into a render crash
samples.evidence: `fileUrl` (packages/frontend/src/api/files.ts:23) is now `seg(documentId)`, which throws for `.`/`..`. Unlike every other `seg` consumer (async API functions whose rejection is handled by react-query/`.catch`), `fileUrl` is called during render at packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139 and packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:726. React-router percent-decodes route params, so a link like `/f/%2E%2E` yields `documentId === ".."` and the throw escapes render (blank screen / error boundary) instead of the previous 404 fetch. The two call sites, not `seg`, are where the handling needs to change (or `fileUrl` should return an empty/invalid URL rather than throw).

samples.summary: Dry-run branches now throw from outside the command's own try/catch, so the error envelope only appears when the CLI is driven through `runCli`
samples.evidence: `seg()`/`printDryRun` now throw, and several dry-run branches sit *outside* the handler's try/catch: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:135 and :155, packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:95/:115, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:100/:120, packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:124/:144. In production this is caught by `runCli` (packages/cli/src/cli.ts:90), so behaviour is fine there — but any embedder or test that calls `program.parseAsync` directly (as packages/cli/test/dry-run.test.ts does) gets a raw rejection rather than the documented `{error:{code,message}}` envelope, which is a contract difference between the two entry points introduced by this change.

finding.summary: New image-fetch guard aborts the whole docs PDF/DOCX export when one image is refused — the exporters have no per-image catch
finding.evidence: `collectAndEmbedImages` (packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:57) does `const blob = await fetcher(src);` inside the loop with no try/catch, and `DocxExporter.export` does the same at packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:76. `createImageFetcher` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261) now *throws* for any image whose host is non-public or whose scheme is not http/https/data, where previously it only threw on a non-OK HTTP status. So a self-hosted install serving blobs from an internal host (MinIO, a second port on the API box), or a doc carrying an intranet/`file:`-style `src` from an import, turns `wafflebase docs export` from "PDF with a missing/failed image" into "whole export fails" — and the CLI has no `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS` set by default. Note the inconsistency: the slides PDF path *does* swallow per-image failures (packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:282-284), so the same guarded refusal degrades gracefully there and is fatal in docs. Fix belongs either in the new fetcher (skip vs. throw policy) or in the docs exporters.

verdict.reason: All substantive claims verified in the working tree. packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:57 awaits `fetcher(src)` inside a bare for-loop (lines 56-74) with no try/catch, so any rejection aborts the whole embed map. packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:73-82 wraps the fetcher in try/`finally` (progress only, no catch, re-throws) and the actual call at :428 is uncaught, awaited from `export` at :87/:102/:114. packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts now throws before any HTTP request: scheme refusal at :198-202, private-host refusal at :206-211, unresolvable-name refusal at :263-267 and resolves-to-private at :270-276, all run via `guard` at :299-307 before the first fetch (:311) and on every redirect (:356) — strictly earlier and broader than the pre-existing non-OK-status throw at :338-342. The CLI builds the fetcher with only `serverBase` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261-263) so `allowedHosts` defaults to an empty `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS` (image-fetcher.ts:296-297, :42-50); the code's own comments (:36-41, :170-175) confirm the split-origin self-hosted case is real and reachable. The throw propagates to the CLI catch at packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:310-312, so writeBinary (:309) never runs — the whole export fails rather than producing a doc with one missing image. The cited asymmetry is real: packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:281-286 catches per-image failures and substitutes BLANK_PNG. This is squarely in the blast-radius lane — a behaviour/contract change to an exported symbol whose consumers in another package were not updated, and the fix belongs at the unupdated consumers (or as a skip-vs-throw policy in the new fetcher). Only inaccuracy is cosmetic: the docx line cited as :76 is the catch-less progress wrapper; the real fetch is :428. No named refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and it is not another lens's issue.

finding.summary: `seg()` makes `fileUrl` throw synchronously inside a React render path, turning a bad route id into a render crash
finding.evidence: `fileUrl` (packages/frontend/src/api/files.ts:23) is now `seg(documentId)`, which throws for `.`/`..`. Unlike every other `seg` consumer (async API functions whose rejection is handled by react-query/`.catch`), `fileUrl` is called during render at packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139 and packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:726. React-router percent-decodes route params, so a link like `/f/%2E%2E` yields `documentId === ".."` and the throw escapes render (blank screen / error boundary) instead of the previous 404 fetch. The two call sites, not `seg`, are where the handling needs to change (or `fileUrl` should return an empty/invalid URL rather than throw).

verdict.reason: The code exists as described (seg() throws for './..' at url.ts:18-23; fileUrl() is sync at files.ts:22-25; called in render at pdf-collab.tsx:139 and shared-document.tsx:726), but the render path is unreachable for a dot-segment id. On the `/f/:id` route (App.tsx:127 -> FileDetail), the URL-bar id is first passed to the async fetchDocument (file-detail.tsx:191), which itself calls seg(id) at documents.ts:47; the synchronous throw inside the async function becomes a rejected react-query promise, and file-detail.tsx:198/204 render a Loader then `<Navigate to="/documents" replace/>` before PdfFileLayout/PdfCollabProvider (and thus fileUrl) ever mounts. The other render call site (shared-document.tsx:667 and :726) receives `resolved.documentId`, which is server-returned from resolveShareLink (share-links.ts:99-111, ResolvedShareLink at :15-16), not a route param. The one theoretical window — `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` (file-detail.tsx:195) permitting a single render with a not-yet-validated id on an in-app key change — requires a client-side navigation to a dot id, but all in-app `/f/:id` navigations use server-supplied ids via getDocumentPath (document-list.tsx:437,1471,1480; notification-text.ts:40), and a pasted/typed URL is a full document load with no previous data, which takes the guarded path. All other fileUrl consumers (image-viewer.tsx:38, image-thumb.tsx:26, download-file.ts:59) are async/effect paths.

finding.summary: `seg()` makes the synchronous `fileUrl()` throwable, and it is called during React render with no ErrorBoundary anywhere in the frontend
finding.evidence: `fileUrl(documentId, token)` is evaluated in the body of `PdfCollabProvider` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139) while building its context value; `documentId` is a route param (`packages/frontend/src/app/files/file-detail.tsx:209` passes `id!` from the router). Every other `seg()` call site added by this diff sits inside an `async` API function, so the throw surfaces as a rejected promise a query can render as an error state — this one throws synchronously during render. A grep for `ErrorBoundary|errorElement` across `packages/frontend/src` returns nothing, so an id of `.`/`..` (reachable as `/f/%2E%2E`, which the browser does not normalize and react-router percent-decodes into the param) unmounts the whole tree instead of showing a not-found state. Other sync call sites with the same shape: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:726`. Fix belongs on the new code — either keep `fileUrl` total (encode without throwing) or guard the id where it enters the route.

verdict.reason: The mechanics are as described (seg() throws on "."/".." at api/url.ts:18-23; fileUrl() is sync at api/files.ts:22-25 and is evaluated in render at app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139; no ErrorBoundary exists in packages/frontend/src), but the claimed reachable vector is guarded before the render ever happens. On /f/:id, FileDetail first fetches the document via useQuery (file-detail.tsx:185-196); fetchDocument is async and calls seg(id) internally (api/documents.ts:45-48), so a "."/".." id yields a rejected promise, not a sync throw. FileDetail then returns early on docError with <Navigate to="/documents" replace /> (file-detail.tsx:198-204, with an explicit comment that a failed fetch must not fall through to the PDF layout), so PdfFileLayout/PdfCollabProvider — and therefore fileUrl() — is never rendered with a dot id. The cited file-detail.tsx:209 is ImageFileLayout, whose fileUrl call is inside an async effect (image-viewer.tsx:38), not render. The other "sync call site", shared-document.tsx:726 (and the shared PdfCollabProvider at :666), uses resolved.documentId returned by the server's share-link resolve, not a URL param; the URL-controlled token there goes through seg() inside the async resolveShareLink (api/share-links.ts:103). The only residual window (placeholderData: keepPreviousData at file-detail.tsx:195 during in-app navigation) would require the server itself to return a document id of "." — in-app /f/${id} links are built from server data (document-list-utils.ts:162, image-viewer.tsx:103) — and cannot be triggered by typing /f/%2E%2E, which is a full page load with no previous data.

mergedFrom.summary: New `assertFetchableImageUrl` host guard can break existing `docs export` / `slides export` runs against self-hosted or split-origin deployments

finding.summary: The new image-host guard uses exact origin equality against `--server`, but the frontend persists ABSOLUTE image URLs into document content, so existing docs can stop exporting on any self-hosted/dev origin mismatch
finding.evidence: `resolveImageUrl` in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:127-129 rewrites every backend image URL to absolute before it is written into the CRDT ("EVERY path that writes a backend image URL into a CRDT document has to apply this"), so stored `src` values are e.g. `http://localhost:3000/images/...` in dev and whatever `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is in a self-hosted install. `assertFetchableImageUrl` exempts such a URL only via `sameOriginAsServer` (string origin equality) or `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS`. Any alias mismatch between the browser's API origin and the CLI's configured `server` — `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`, http vs https, a second port, or a private-IP API host reached under a different name — now makes the previously-working `docs export` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261) and `slides export` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209) fail with "non-public address" for documents that used to embed fine. Consumers of `createImageFetcher` outside the diff inherit this without change.

verdict.reason: All claimed code exists as described. `sameOriginAsServer` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:142-148) is literal string origin equality and is the only automatic exemption used by assertFetchableImageUrl (image-fetcher.ts:204-211) and assertResolvedHostIsPublic (image-fetcher.ts:251-252); a private/loopback host that is not origin-identical to `--server` throws "non-public address". The frontend really does persist absolute backend URLs into document content: resolveImageUrl (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:127-131) prefixes VITE_BACKEND_API_URL and its result is stored via uploadImageFile (image-upload.ts:58) by board-image.ts:12, notes-detail.tsx:141, slides-detail.tsx:313/655, sheet-view.tsx:504, with the parallel docs path at export-utils.ts:12-18,39. The CLI export consumers outside the guard file, docs.ts:261-263 and slides.ts:209, pass getConfig(opts).server, resolved independently from flags/env/session/profile/DEFAULT_SERVER (config/config.ts:7,77-167) — no mechanism ties it to the browser's VITE_BACKEND_API_URL. So any alias mismatch on a private host (localhost vs 127.0.0.1, second port, intranet name for a private-IP API host) makes previously-working exports fail. WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS (README.md:46) is a manual operator opt-out, not a guard that makes the regression unreachable. In-lane for blast radius: a behaviour change to an exported symbol affecting persisted data written by another package and CLI callers the diff does not show; impact = major.
